title: Certified Policy Optimisation for Nested Causal Bandits via PAC-Bayes Risk
claim: A hierarchical causal problem class, its recursive sampling algorithm, and a certificate-gated deployment rule fit together as one system.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right: causal graph, nested-box algorithm, certified-gain plot
description: Three side-by-side panels titled (a) NCCB, (b) NCTS and (c) AEGIS. Panel (a) is a causal DAG. A dashed black circle U is the latent confounder, drawn with grey dashed arrows. Meta-context C(2) is a black square and meta-action A(2) is a blue square. Inner context C(1) is a green circle, and A(1) is an orange circle filled pink. Y and R are green circles. Green arrows show learnable mechanisms, and blue and orange arrows show policy decisions. Panel (b) is a grey box. It holds a blue meta-level box (C(2) → A(2)) above an orange inner-level box (C(1) → A(1) → Y,R). A green arrow labelled P(C(1)|C(2),A(2)) links them. Text above and below the box describes drawing a belief and then updating the posterior. Panel (c) is a line plot of certified gain lower bound against episodes K. A blue median line sits inside a shaded min-to-max band. A thick red bar at zero marks where the gate fires. The eye goes first to the colourful DAG on the left.
caption: The NCCB framework at a glance ($L\!=\!2$). (\subref{fig:banner-dag}) Hierarchical SCM problem class: meta-context $C^{(2)}$ drives meta-action $A^{(2)}$ ($\ell\!=\!2$); together they set the inner context $C^{(1)}$ for the inner action $A^{(1)}$, producing outcome $Y$ and reward $R$. (\subref{fig:banner-ncts}) NCTS (Algorithm [ref]) draws one belief per episode and acts recursively across levels, with $I_2$ meta steps and $I_2\!\times\!I_1$ inner steps; after the episode, the posterior is updated. (\subref{fig:banner-bench}) AEGIS deploys NCTS only after the per-level PRISM certificate (Theorem [ref]) flips, realising the progressive certified handover the framework targets. On the two-level \bench{Crossing} bench (10 seeds, $\delta\!=\!0.05$, posterior still learning, gate suppressed), the leaf-level certified-gain lower bound (LB; median; band: min to max over seeds) first crosses $0$, where the gate would fire, between $K\!=\!3{,}000$ and $16{,}000$ (red bar: spread of first crossings over seeds) and reaches $+25.7$ to $+42.9$ by $K\!=\!52{,}000$; on $4$ of the $10$ seeds it dips below $0$ at least once before staying positive (App. [ref]). Visual encoding in (a, b): blue/orange, policy decisions; green, learnable mechanisms; grey dashed, latent confounder.
abstract: Critical sequential decisions are rarely single-timescale: a strategic decision causally shapes the context in which every subsequent tactical choice is made; standard bandit and reinforcement-learning theory does not capture this causal coupling between timescales. We formalise the problem class as Nested Contextual Causal Bandits (NCCBs), a hierarchical SCM where each level's action sets the next level's context distribution, and propose Nested Causal Thompson Sampling (NCTS), which draws one mechanism-factorised belief per episode and acts recursively under it. Our main theoretical result is a causal PAC-Bayesian excess-risk bound that certifies any candidate deployment policy from historic data alone, off-policy and anytime, answering the deployment question: can we trust this agent here, and at what risk? Experiments on a hierarchical SCM show that, against a matched RFF-GP joint regression on the same function class, the factorised SCM-mechanism posterior transfers significantly better zero-shot under exogenous distribution shifts, the recursive meta-to-inner commit significantly dominates the joint-commit alternative in distribution, and the certificate significantly contracts as offline data accumulates. Combining these results, we establish progressive certified handover, a safe-deployment method: each timescale flips from a legacy controller to NCTS when gains can be certified, independently of the others.
